description:
OBSOLETED on 2026-04-26: superseded by the single-repo migration plan
(_project/TODO/main/planning/single-repo-migration-phase-*.yaml). The
release guide is still produced, but as part of the single-repo
migration's Phase 7 (docs cleanup), describing a much simpler flow
(Makefile + GitHub Actions release workflow). The original version
of this TODO described the guide for the old two-repo orchestration,
which no longer exists post-migration.

Original deps removed (the two depended-on TODOs were also obsoleted
the same day).

Original description below preserved for historical context.

---

Release knowledge today is fragmented across:
- `scripts/automate_release.py` docstring (developer-facing, not skimmable)
- `AGENTS.md` (mixed agent guidance)
- `docs/development/development.md:99` (a stub: "Release Preparation Workflow")
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:193` ("Releases are handled by maintainers" - points
  nowhere)

A maintainer cutting their first BenchBox release has nowhere coherent to
look. The new guide is the canonical entrypoint: skimmable, ~1500 words,
links to source for detail.

Why this depends on the other two items: the doc references the new
`is_public_path` predicate (in the glossary) and the new `Step 3.5`
divergence preflight + `--allow-public-divergence` flag (in the failure
recovery section). Writing it before those land would produce stale docs.

Format and location confirmed by the existing precedent: `docs/operations/`
already houses `results-phase-2-runbook.md` (a sibling maintainer runbook),
myst-parser markdown is the project default.

Plan file: /Users/joe/.claude/plans/make-a-detailed-and-dynamic-bentley.md
(Phase C).

anti_patterns.dont: add a "history" or "previous release process" section
anti_patterns.why: it is dead weight; the guide describes how to release TODAY, full stop.

anti_patterns.dont: duplicate content from automate_release.py's docstring into the guide
anti_patterns.why: the docstring is for developers reading the source; the guide is for maintainers running the tool; they need different framings. Link to source, summarise behaviour, do not paste.
the existing docs are text-only and screenshots rot fast; ASCII tables and code blocks are sufficient and maintainable.

anti_patterns.dont: make the guide a complete reference of every flag
anti_patterns.why: that is what `--help` is for; the guide is the runbook ("here is what to do"), not the man page.

anti_patterns.dont: write the guide before the dependent items land
anti_patterns.why: it references the new is_public_path predicate and the new --allow-public-divergence flag; writing first means rewriting twice.

preserves.behavior: Existing anchor `#release-preparation-workflow` in docs/development/development.md continues to resolve (heading kept, body replaced with redirect).
The `AGENTS.md` content is unchanged. The release guide may LINK to it (e.g., for dependency bounds policy) but does not duplicate its content.
The existing `docs/operations/results-phase-2-runbook.md` continues to resolve in the toctree. The new entry is added BEFORE it, not in place of it.
The line at `CONTRIBUTING.md:193` ("Releases are handled by maintainers") remains - optionally extend to add a link to the new guide, but do not remove the existing copy.

work_units.notes:
Create `docs/operations/release-guide.md`. Structure:

  # Cutting a BenchBox release

  ## Overview
  One short diagram: private -> curated public tree -> squash -> tag ->
  wheel -> archive. Plain text or simple ASCII, not a graphics file.

  ## Before you start
  - On private main, clean, fetched.
  - ../BenchBox-public clone exists, on main, clean, fetched.
  - PyPI token configured.
  - The two-remote rule (CLAUDE.md): push to `private`, never `public`
    without intent.

  ## The one command
  ```bash
  uv run python scripts/automate_release.py --version 0.2.2 -y --push
  ```
  What each phase does, with one-liner descriptions and source pointers
  (e.g., "Phase 4 builds the curated public tree - see
  benchbox/release/workflow.py::prepare_public_release").

  ## What automation handles vs what you handle
  Two-column table.
  Automation: version bump, changelog, CI, content checks, size guard,
  public divergence preflight, squash, tag, build, archive.
  You: write user-facing changelog blurb, decide patch vs minor,
  communicate the release.

  ## Recovering from common failures
  - CI check fails -> fix on private, re-run.
  - Size check fails -> identify file, add to HOLD_BACK_PATHS or shrink.
  - Content validation fails (em-dash etc.) -> fix in source, re-run.
  - **Public divergence preflight fails** -> run `benchbox-sync pull
    --revspec <last-tag>..HEAD`, commit on private, re-run. Use
    `--allow-public-divergence` ONLY if you intentionally want to
    overwrite those commits.

  ## When to use benchbox-sync (and when not to)
  Table:
  | Subcommand | Use when |
  | status | Sanity check before release. |
  | pull | An external PR landed on public; bring it back to private. |
  | push | Almost never - prefer cutting a patch release. |

  ## Glossary
  - Squash anchor - previous v* tag, where the next release squashes from.
  - Normalized timestamp - most-recent-whole-hour UTC.
  - Source fingerprint - hash of the curated tree.
  - Curated tree - the subset decided by `is_public_path` (single-source
    predicate in benchbox/release/workflow.py).

  ## Reference
  - Source: `scripts/automate_release.py`, `benchbox/release/workflow.py`,
    `benchbox/release/sync.py`.
  - Related: AGENTS.md (dependency bounds), CONTRIBUTING.md.

Style: myst-parser markdown (.md). Triple-backtick fences with language
hints. H2 sentence case. Frontmatter copyright header consistent with
other docs/operations/*.md files - check
`docs/operations/results-phase-2-runbook.md` and copy the header style.
Length target: ~1500 words. If it grows past 2500, split.

Run:
  cd docs && uv run -- python -m sphinx -W -b html . _build/html
Must complete with zero warnings. The `-W` flag converts warnings to
errors, so any unresolved cross-reference, broken toctree entry, or
myst parse error fails the build.
Then open `docs/_build/html/operations/release-guide.html` in a
browser and visually confirm:
  - Code blocks render with syntax highlighting
  - Internal links resolve (especially the dev-doc redirect from w3)
  - The toctree shows the new page in the Contributing section
Spot-check on a phone or narrow window for the table layout
(the "automation vs you" two-column table is the most likely to wrap
awkwardly).
